rationale: The candidate reads as one primary sectional gesture: a compact stacked platform mass with a lateral slide, visible in all four views. The massing is coherent and not overly fragmented, with a clear main volume and smaller support offsets. It avoids depending purely on a stair-step skyline, though the terracing is still the dominant formal device. The void logic is weak: there is only a modest undercut/slot rather than a substantial courtyard or public opening, so the form feels mostly solid. Repair integrity is strong because the volumes appear consistently aligned across views without obvious collisions or accidental clipping. The precedent resonance is credible with OMA/BIG-style shifted platforms and terraced sectional massing, but it remains a generic diagram rather than a distinct reinterpretation.
warnings: Void/public space is limited; the form reads more as stacked solids than as a mass with a meaningful open ground condition.
The silhouette is still terrace-led, so the next iteration should reduce dependence on stepped offsets if a stronger non-stair identity is desired.
